newsitem.title: EGYPT: Palestinians refuse to go back to Libya.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians refuse to go back to Libya.

text.p: More than 200 Palestinian refugees who have been stranded on the Libyan-Egyptian border for more than a year refused on Tuesday to go back to Libya.
The refugees, deported to the camp in 1995, argued with Libyan officials who tried to persuade them back, saying they would rather go to Egypt or the Palestinian self-rule areas.
"We want to go to any Arab country other than Libya. We want to go to Palestine. There are 15,000 Palestinians in Libya who are unemployed," one Palestinian man told Libyan officials.

The refugess and members of staff with the international charity Medecins sans Frontieres who are permanently based in the camp asked journalists not to leave because they feared Libyan officials would use force against the Palestinians.

Libya threw them out in 1995 in an attempt to discredit steps towards peace between Israel and the Palestinians. Egypt will not let them in unless they can prove a third country will give them residence.

Some refugees have been living for more than a year in appalling conditions in a tented encampment in no-man's-land between the Egyptian and Libyan border posts. Libya reversed the policy a week ago, saying it was not possible for the Palestinians to go home to the Palestinian-ruled territories.
